### **Vanguard Lifter** (Utility Exoframe — Vanguard Systems)

The Power Loader of NYTE City — yellow industrial exoframe, open operator station, bipedal, and built to move things that human beings cannot. The Lifter is the mech that construction crews operate, that disaster response teams deploy, that dock workers use to shift cargo containers at the Port Authority terminals. It is common enough on work sites that passing one registers as background detail rather than a notable event.

Three tool mounts replace the weapon systems of combat mechs: standard configuration includes Loader Jaws rated for structural steel, an articulated Cutting Torch capable of demolition-grade cutting, and a Crane Arm with a rated lift capacity of fifteen metric tons. The operator station is open — a cab-style seat within the frame rather than a sealed cockpit. This is fine on a construction site. In a firefight the operator is exposed.

The Lifter's durability reflects industrial design rather than combat engineering. It was built to operate in environments where things fall on it, where it works in conditions that would damage less robust hardware, and where it needs to keep functioning through a full work shift without maintenance stops. It was not built to take weapons fire. It handles weapons fire considerably better than it has any right to, because Vanguard builds things that last.

Using a Lifter in combat is improvisation. The Loader Jaws that move cargo pallets can close around a person. The Cutting Torch rated for structural demolition does not care what it is cutting. The Crane Arm has leverage sufficient to throw objects — or people — significant distances. None of this is what the Lifter was designed for. It is, however, available to whoever is desperate enough to be sitting in one when things go wrong.

#### Tool Mounts (standard configuration):

- Loader Jaws — Rated for structural steel; improvised weapon (Massive damage, melee range)

- Cutting Torch — Demolition-grade; improvised weapon (Energy damage, Burning, melee range)

- Crane Arm — Heavy lift; improvised throw or grapple at range

*Note: The open operator station means the pilot is not protected by the mech's PROT/RES against attacks that specifically target the operator position.*

**\**

### **Salvage Frame** (Retrofitted Utility Mech — Various)

Someone got hold of a Lifter — or something like a Lifter — and decided it wasn't enough. Salvaged armor panels welded to the frame. One tool mount converted or replaced with something more aggressive. The open cockpit partially enclosed with whatever plate was available. The result is not a combat mech. It is not quite a utility mech either. It is something the city didn't plan for, which in NYTE City is its own kind of advantage.

The Salvage Frame's lower Integrity percentage reflects the improvised nature of its construction — the modifications are not engineered, they are applied, and under sustained stress the joins show. The armor panels protect better than an unmodified Lifter but sit below anything purpose-built for combat. The one weapon or heavy tool mount retained from the base frame makes it more dangerous than it looks, which given that it looks like a welding project gone wrong, is saying something.

No two Salvage Frames are identical. Some retain the Loader Jaws and add a salvaged beam weapon to the shoulder. Some convert the Cutting Torch mount to carry a belt-fed heavy weapon and cover the cockpit with recycled vehicle armor. Some are melee specialists — the Loader Jaws reinforced, the frame stripped of everything that doesn't contribute to closing distance and hitting hard. The stat block represents a typical example. The specific capabilities depend on who built it and what they had.

Cost and availability are listed as — because Salvage Frames are not purchased. They are built, commissioned from someone who knows how, or acquired from whoever built the last one and no longer needs it. Stats represent a typical example — actual capabilities vary considerably.

**\**

### **Vanguard Warden** (All-Purpose Combat Mech — Vanguard Systems)

The Warden is what Vanguard makes when the job requires a mech rather than a vehicle. The same design philosophy that produces the Sentinel battle rifle and the Ironwall HMG produces a combat platform built to operate across the full range of environments a professional operator might encounter — urban, industrial, open terrain, and everything in between. Balanced PROT and RES, sealed cockpit, two Light weapon mounts on the arms, and four mod slots that reflect Vanguard's understanding that operators have specific requirements that a general-purpose chassis needs to accommodate.

The Warden's civilian variants — construction, search and rescue, infrastructure maintenance — share the same chassis with different tool packages installed in the weapon mount positions. A crew that encounters a Warden in a work zone and a Warden in a combat zone is looking at the same machine configured for different purposes. Vanguard considers this a feature. So do operators who have used a construction Warden to do something a construction Warden was not supposed to do.

The four mod slots are the Warden's defining characteristic relative to the other combat chassis. The Phantom hits harder and moves faster. The Colossus survives more. The Warden can be either of those things, or something between them, depending on what the operator installs. It is the platform that rewards investment and punishes neglect — a fully kitted Warden is competitive with anything on this list in its configured role; a stock Warden is competitive with nothing in particular but adequate across everything.

#### Standard Systems:

- Class II Combat System Package (helmet)

- Gyro Stabilizers — +2 to Pilot checks to maintain balance

- Environmental Seal — Full life support and air filtration

- Two Light weapon mounts (arm-mounted, belt-fed or power cell)

**\**

### **Vanguard Warden-C** (Civic Control Mech — Vanguard Systems)

The C in Warden-C stands for Civic. Law enforcement knows what that means. The press calls it the Civic model. Neither name is wrong, and Vanguard's product literature never uses the words "riot control" anywhere in the official documentation.

The Warden-C is a standard Warden chassis with all four mod slots configured for crowd management systems rather than combat weapons. The Sonic Dispersal Array produces a directional acoustic effect that is technically non-lethal at specified operational parameters. The Water Cannon delivers sufficient force to knock an unarmored person down at range. The Tear Gas Launchers cover the same area as three EG-3 Blackout grenades simultaneously. The Restraint Net Launcher immobilizes targets at short range. The Crowd Barrier Arms extend the mech's physical reach for containment and redirection of crowds. The Riot Shield Panel deploys from the forearm, providing additional frontal protection and a surface that is, at mech scale, approximately the size of a small vehicle.

The tension in the Warden-C is not in what it is designed to do, but rather the scale in which it operates. A sonic dispersal system that disperses a crowd of twenty people is operating exactly as specified. The experience of being in that crowd is something different. NYTE City’s law enforcement agencies maintain Warden-C units for large-scale civil unrest operations, major event security, and situations where the presence of a twelve-foot civic control platform is considered a proportionate response. Who decides what constitutes a proportionate response is a political question the equipment chapter declines to answer.

The Warden-C is available by contract to law enforcement agencies, licensed private security firms, and — through channels that Vanguard maintains are rigorously vetted — certain corporate clients with documented crowd management requirements. The 40,000Ç premium over the base Warden reflects the specialized systems package. The package itself can be removed and replaced with standard Light mounts, converting a Warden-C back to a Warden. Vanguard notes this capability in their sales materials. They don’t elaborate on why they consider it worth mentioning.

#### Civic Mounts (standard configuration):

- Sonic Dispersal Array — Area Stun, wide cone, non-lethal at spec

- Water Cannon — Knockdown, short range, non-lethal

- Tear Gas Launchers — Gas area denial, equivalent to three simultaneous EG-3 grenades

- Restraint Net Launcher — Immobilizes target, short range

#### Additional Civic Mount options (installed at purchase):

- Crowd Barrier Arms — Extended physical containment and redirection

- Riot Shield Panel — Deployable frontal shield, +4 PROT against frontal attacks

**\**

### **Enigma Phantom** (Scout/Striker Combat Mech — Enigma Defense Technologies)

Enigma Defense built the Phantom around a specific tactical premise: that the most dangerous combat asset is one the enemy doesn't see coming and cannot catch when it leaves. The Phantom is the fastest mech on this list by a significant margin, carries more weapons than anything at its armor class has any right to, and sacrifices survivability for the ability to dictate every engagement on its own terms. It arrives fast, hits hard, and leaves before the response can organize.

The lower RES reflects composite armor optimized for weight reduction rather than maximum protection — the Phantom is not designed to stand in a sustained firefight. It is designed to make sustained firefights unnecessary. Two Light mounts and one Heavy mount give it strike capability that would be excessive on a slower platform; on the Phantom it is the point. An operator who uses a Phantom by standing still and trading hits with a Colossus has fundamentally misunderstood what they are piloting.

The advanced stealth systems and sensor suite reflect Enigma's intelligence-operations background — the Phantom knows more about its environment than it reveals about itself. Rare availability means Enigma sells to vetted clients through a process that the company describes as thorough and most people describe as intrusive.

#### Standard Systems:

- Class III Combat System Package (helmet)

- Advanced Sensor Suite — Enhanced detection and targeting

- Stealth Systems — Reduced acoustic and visual signature

- Gyro Stabilizers — +2 to Pilot checks to maintain balance

- Environmental Seal — Full life support and air filtration

- Two Light weapon mounts + one Heavy mount

**\**

### **Hammerlock Colossus** (Juggernaut Combat Mech — Hammerlock, Inc.)

There is no diplomatic way to describe what the Colossus is. It is a siege engine in bipedal form — maximum armor, maximum firepower, minimum concern for anything that isn't its primary objective. The Colossus moves at 25 km/h because that is fast enough to get where it is going, and because nothing at that speed and that armor class needs to move faster. It arrives. Things stop being problems. It leaves.

The 1d12 PROT and +14 RES put it in a category where most personal weapons are irrelevant against it. Anti-materiel rifles and rocket launchers are required equipment for anyone tasked with stopping a Colossus — standard heavy weapons will chip its INT over a very long time, if the operator survives long enough to notice. Two Heavy mounts and one Siege mount represent ordnance that would be excessive on anything else on this list. On the Colossus, it is standard configuration.

Hammerlock sells the Colossus by contract to specific clients for specific purposes. The contract process is not published. The clients are not listed. What is known is that certain factions in NYTE City have Colossus units, which tells anyone paying attention something significant about those factions and the people they have relationships with. When a Colossus appears in a scene it is not a combat encounter. It is a weather event that the GM has decided the crew needs to deal with.

#### Standard Systems:

- Class IV Combat System Package (helmet)

- Reinforced Joint Systems — Reduced System Failure chance for limb results

- Grounding Net — Electrical surge protection

- EMP Shielding — Resistance to EMP-triggered system failures

- Environmental Seal — Full life support, air filtration, NBC protection

- Two Heavy weapon mounts + one Siege mount

# Combat System Packages

Every powered armor suit and mech chassis in this chapter references a Combat System Package — the bundled sensor, HUD, and communications suite installed in the helmet or cockpit. These packages determine what information the operator has access to, what systems they can interface with, and how effectively the suit's capabilities can be utilized.

Four classes of package exist. Higher classes add capability rather than replacing lower-class features — a Class IV system does everything a Class I does, plus significantly more. The class designation is a ceiling, not a list of exclusive features.

#### Feature Definitions

Full descriptions of every Combat System Package feature are provided below for reference.

**Advanced HUD** — Inside most powered suits and mech cockpits there is a standard Heads Up Display. The Advanced HUD is capable of working with onboard AI through complex interactive systems, allowing seamless use of all suit or vehicle systems. Reactive marquis displays change based on operational necessity. Supports targeting from linked weapon systems.

**Audio Dampers** — Dulls the sound of gunfire, explosions, and other loud combat sounds to protect the operator's hearing and prevent disorientation. Operators with Audio Dampers cannot become Disoriented from proximity to explosions or sustained loud sounds.

**Basic HUD** — A bare-necessities display offering system status output, video communication marquis, navigational assistance, and targeting support from linked devices. Cannot support AI integration. Fixed marquis displays do not adapt to changing conditions.

**Compartments** — Internal and external storage compartments for ammunition, equipment, and supplies. Depending on configuration may include hidden holsters, armored pockets, and sealed storage for sensitive materials.

**E-Chrome** — Electro-chromatic surface coating that responds to electrical current. Used for camouflage through color shifting, one-way opacity for transparent surfaces, or aesthetic customization. Most effective on vehicles and powered suits.

**Emergency Beacon** — Encrypted distress signal transmitting location and vitals status to a predetermined receiver via satellite or LINK relay. Activation is automatic when vitals drop to critical threshold or manual via panic input. Encrypted at TECH TN8 TH4 to breach via LINK; terminal breach at difficulty 28 (Interface).

**Enhanced Audio** — Advanced directional audio processing that grants a bonus to audio-based Awareness checks. Filters environmental noise while amplifying relevant sounds.

**Flash Down** — Optical protection against bright light sources and dazzle weapons. Operators with Flash Down cannot become Disoriented from light-based attacks or environmental glare.

**Gyro Stabilizers** — Automated balance correction systems. Grants +2 to Athletics or Pilot checks when attempting to maintain or recover balance.

**IFF** — Friend-or-foe identification system that tags identified friendlies and hostiles in the HUD. Reduces friendly fire risk in complex engagements.

**Land NAV** — Visual overlay displaying designated navigation points and optimal routing to objectives. Enhanced version adds predictive routing and obstacle mapping.

**LR Radio** — Long-range radio communications beyond the range of standard Trans-Communications arrays. Used for coordination across large operational areas or when standard comm infrastructure is unavailable.

**Magnetic Stow Points** — Magnetized mounting points on the suit exterior for hands-free equipment storage. Items stored this way can be drawn as a free action in combat.

**Motion Detector** — Detects motion within sensor range and displays position data in the Advanced HUD. Effective against targets attempting to use cover or concealment.

**Night Vision** — Full visibility in pitch darkness without penalty to any checks.

**Onboard Camera** — Helmet or cockpit-mounted camera for recording and streaming. Used for intelligence gathering, evidence collection, and remote observation.

**Radar System** — Active radar with a range of up to 600 meters. Displays contacts regardless of visual conditions. Active radar is detectable by opponents with appropriate sensor equipment.

**Rainbow Sights** — Full spectrum visual optics with selectable modes including UV, infrared, and standard visible light. Allows operators to see in conditions that would blind standard optics.

**Readout: Marquis** — Holographic overlay for detecting and reading hidden holographic signals, environmental data tags, and AR information layers embedded in the environment.

**Readout: Vitals** — Real-time biometric monitoring of the pilot displayed in the HUD. Tracks heart rate, stress indicators, injury status, and other health metrics. Integrates with uDoc Module for automated medical response.

**SMART Link** — AI targeting link between the operator and SMART-compatible weapons. Provides +1 to aimed and burst shots. Requires compatible weapons to function.

**Spectrum Optics** — Advanced environmental analysis through visual spectrum manipulation. Identifies materials, detects hazards, and provides enhanced environmental awareness beyond standard Rainbow Sights.

**Telescopics** — Up to 25× zoom capability on digital video feeds. Used for extreme-range target identification and observation.

**Threat Assessment** — Combat computer that continuously assesses, categorizes, and prioritizes threats in the operator's environment. Displays threat data in the Advanced HUD.

**Tight Beam Comms** — Hyper-stable and highly secure communications array for sensitive transmissions. Significantly harder to intercept or jam than standard Trans-Communications.

**Tracking System** — Location beacon integrated into the suit for command tracking and coordination. Can be used for search and rescue or as a target marker for allied forces.

**Trans-Communications** — Standard communications array for fireteam and field operations coordination. The baseline communications system for all combat platforms.

## Class I System Package

The baseline combat package. Everything an operator needs to function in a contested environment without any of the advanced targeting or sensor capabilities of higher classes. Class I systems are found in first-generation powered armor, older mech chassis, and platforms built for operators who prioritize cost over capability.

#### Standard Features:

- **Basic HUD** — System status, video communications, navigational overlay, and linked weapon targeting. Fixed marquis displays that do not adapt to changing conditions.

- **Compartments** — Internal and external storage for ammunition, equipment, and supplies.

- **Emergency Beacon** — Encrypted distress signal transmitting location and vitals to a predetermined receiver. Hackable with sufficient skill.

- **Night Vision** — Full visibility in pitch darkness without penalty.

- **Tracking System** — Location beacon for command and coordination purposes.

- **Trans-Communications** — Standard fireteam communications array for field operations.

## Class II System Package

The standard package for most operational platforms. Adds navigational, visual spectrum, and information display capabilities over the Class I baseline. The Vanguard Warden ships with Class II as standard — sufficient for most professional applications without the cost overhead of the advanced packages.

#### All Class I features, plus:

- **Land NAV** — Visual overlay for navigating to designated waypoints and objectives.

- **Magnetic Stow Points** — Magnetized storage points on the armor exterior for hands-free weapon and equipment stowage. Items stored this way can be drawn as a free action.

- **Rainbow Sights** — Full spectrum visual optics including UV and infrared modes.

- **Readout: Marquis** — Overlay display for hidden holographic signals and environmental data.

## Class III System Package

The professional standard. Class III adds active threat detection, advanced audio processing, and AI targeting integration — the package that most serious combat operators consider the minimum viable configuration. The majority of powered armor entries in this chapter ship with Class III.

#### All Class II features, plus:

- **Advanced HUD** — AI-integrated reactive display system. Supports full diagnostic output, navigational overlays, and seamless weapons system integration. Marquis displays adapt to current operational requirements rather than remaining fixed.

- **Audio Dampers** — Prevents Disoriented condition from proximity to explosions or sustained loud sounds. Protects against sonic weapons and environmental noise hazards.

- **Flash Down** — Optical protection against bright light and dazzle weapons. Prevents Disoriented from flash-based attacks.

- **Motion Detector** — Detects movement and displays hostile positions in the Advanced HUD.

- **SMART Link** — AI targeting link between operator and compatible weapons. +1 to aimed and burst shots with SMART Link active.

- **Threat Assessment** — Combat computer that identifies, categorizes, and prioritizes threats on the battlefield.

#### Choose 2 Optional Features:

- **LR Radio** — Long-range communications beyond standard Trans-Comm range

- **IFF** — Friend-or-foe identification system

- **Readout: Marquis** — Enhanced holographic signal overlay

- **Spectrum Optics** — Advanced environmental analysis through visual spectrum

- **Land NAV (Enhanced)** — Full navigational suite with predictive routing

## Class IV System Package

The most sophisticated combat package available. Class IV adds pilot biometric monitoring, high-magnification optics, and enhanced audio processing over the Class III baseline — the full suite of what current technology can provide to an operator in a powered platform. The Shinsei Renzo X1 ships with Class IV as standard, which represents a significant portion of what makes it the benchmark platform it is.

#### All Class III features, plus:

- **Enhanced Audio** — Significant bonus to audio-based Awareness checks. Directional sound processing and filtering beyond standard Audio Dampers.

- **Readout: Vitals** — Real-time pilot biometric monitoring displayed in the HUD. Integrates with uDoc Module if installed.

- **Telescopics** — Up to 25× zoom on digital video feeds for extreme-range observation and targeting.

- **Land NAV (Enhanced)** — Full navigational suite with predictive routing, obstacle mapping, and waypoint management.

#### Choose 3 Optional Features:

- **E-Chrome** — Electronically responsive surface coating for camouflage, color shifting, or opacity control

- **Gyro Stabilizers** — +2 to relevant Pilot checks to maintain balance

- **Onboard Camera** — Helmet-mounted recording and streaming capability

- **IFF** — Friend-or-foe identification

- **LR Radio** — Long-range communications

- **Radar System** — Active radar up to 600 meters

- **Readout: Marquis** — Enhanced holographic signal overlay

- **Spectrum Optics** — Advanced environmental visual analysis

- **Tight Beam Comms** — Hyper-stable and secure communications array
